scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC3 and PC4 in Campus 2 VLAN 6 report their gateway (10.6.0.254)
no longer responds. Other Campus 2 PCs (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5 on
VLAN 5) are fine. Identify the misconfiguration.

injection.action: change br_v6 SVI IP from .254 to .200
injection.command:
ip addr del 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6
  ip addr add 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v6 SVI IP address
Mechanism: PCs have their default route hard-coded to
  10.6.0.254 (the standard Cisco SVI VRRP-style address).
  sshswitch's br_v6 was reconfigured to 10.6.0.200, so
  ARP for 10.6.0.254 gets no reply — packets can't egress
  the subnet. The new address .200 IS reachable, but no host
  knows to use it.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v6 SVI IP set to 10.6.0.200 instead of 10.6.0.254
Fix: re-set the IP — `ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6 &&
  ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6`
scenario.fix_spec:
re-set the IP — `ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6 &&
  ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: br_v6 SVI IP / VLAN 6 gateway IP

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Campus 2 VLAN 6 Layer-3 SVI on the upstream L3 switch (device “sshswitch”), interface br_v6.

Mechanism: PC3/PC4 have a default route to 10.6.0.254, but no device on VLAN 6 is answering ARP for 10.6.0.254. Their ARP table shows 10.6.0.254 FAILED while 10.6.0.200 resolves and responds. Because the gateway IP they use (10.6.0.254) is absent from the subnet, they cannot reach their gateway, though intra-VLAN connectivity (PC3↔PC4) is fine.

Localization: On sshswitch, VLAN 6 SVI br_v6 is configured with IP 10.6.0.200/24 (evidence: sshswitch ip addr shows “br_v6 … inet 10.6.0.200/24” and MAC 02:95:e3:90:0e:05). PC3’s ARP table shows 10.6.0.200 at that same MAC and is REACHABLE, while 10.6.0.254 is FAILED. Switch4 is pure L2 for VLAN 6 and has no SVI IP, so the L3 gateway must be on sshswitch.

Root cause: The VLAN 6 gateway IP was misconfigured on sshswitch; br_v6 is set to 10.6.0.200 instead of the expected 10.6.0.254.

Corrective fix: Reconfigure sshswitch br_v6 to use 10.6.0.254/24 (replace 10.6.0.200/24). Example: ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6; ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6. After the change, PCs with default via 10.6.0.254 will ARP and reach their gateway. Alternatively, update host default gateways to 10.6.0.200, but aligning with VLAN 5’s .254 convention, fixing the SVI to .254 is recommended. No routing issues upstream were observed.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names and localizes the issue to device 'sshswitch' (br_v6 SVI).

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: br_v6 SVI IP / VLAN 6 gateway IP
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names the VLAN 6 SVI br_v6 on sshswitch and states its IP is 10.6.0.200 (should be 10.6.0.254), satisfying identification of the gateway IP component.
The agent recommends deleting 10.6.0.200 and assigning 10.6.0.254 to br_v6 (or updating hosts), which matches the expected fix and will restore the gateway ARP/responding IP.

The log shows VLAN-6 hosts cannot reach 10.6.0.254 (ARP/ping failures), can reach 10.6.0.200, and the sshswitch was inspected and shows the SVI at .200 — together these observations justify the inference that the SVI was misconfigured to .200. Evidence and reasoning are consistent and the proposed fix follows directly.
